summary: Hideaki Nakatani specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under Gadjin Nagao, was a disciple of Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He was attested as professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.
Hidehiko Kurita specializes in religious studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD from Tohoku University and was attested as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University in 2020.

Hidehiro Okada was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1957) and under Nicholas Poppe at the University of Washington (~1957–1959). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1966–1993) and Tokiwa University (~1996–2002).
Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Delhi. He was attested as a lecturer at Kindai University in 1989.
Hidemasa Nagata was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1952 to 1961 and later held a post there from circa 1967 to 1997.

Hidenaka Tanaka worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1906–1912) under Raphael von Koeber, the University of Oxford (1922–1924), and Kyoto University (PhD 1930). He held posts at Tokyo (~1910–1921), Kyoto University (1920, 1931–1946), and Kyoto Women's University (~1950–1974).

Hidenori Kitagawa was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Hakuju Ui. He was a fellow at the Rockefeller Foundation (1952–1953) and was attested as a professor at Nagoya University (1968–1969).

Hidenori S. Sakuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. His posts include Shitennoji University (attested 1991–1998) and University of Tsukuba (attested 2003–2011).

Hideo Mineshima specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at Taisho University (~1947–1953) and Waseda University (~1953–1956). He held academic posts at Waseda University (1960–1998) and Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1970–1998).

Hideomi Yaita specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1979–1984) and held posts at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1987–1997) and Taisho University (attested 1995).
Hidetaka Fukazawa works in religious studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1976–1980) and held a post at Hitotsubashi University around 1993.
Hidetaka Nakatani works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under Gadjin Nagao.

Hideto Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University from around 1963 to 1967 and served as an associate professor at Aichi Gakuin University from circa 1984 to 1995.

Hidetoshi Yoshizawa works in Buddhist studies. Affiliated with Taisho University, he held posts as a researcher (attested 1998), lecturer (attested 2008), and chief research fellow (attested 2017), alongside studying as a research student at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (attested 2006).

Hidetsugu Yagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909). He held academic posts at Tohoku University (~1919–1930), the University of Tokyo (~1934–1942), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942–1944), and Osaka University (~1946).
Hideyo Ogawa is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He served as an associate professor (~1988–1996) and professor (~1996–2020) at Hiroshima University.

Hideyuki Matsumori specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a doctoral student at Soka University (attested 2006) and later held posts there as assistant professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).

Hilko Wiardo Schomerus was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Paul Deussen at Kiel and Nathan Söderblom at Leipzig. He held teaching posts at Kiel University (1918–1926) and was ord. Professor at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1926.

Himanshu Prabha Ray is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at Panjab, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. She was associate professor at JNU (1980–2012), chair of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015), and honorary professor at the University of Munich (2014–2019).
Hinrich Middeldorpf was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1806–1810) and held a post at the University of Breslau from circa 1813 to 1861.
